All records provisional.

characters.summary: Nakia is a Wakandan War Dog (spy) who works undercover abroad and fights with Ring Blades used as thrown and close-quarters chakrams, plus conventional firearms.

techniques: Firearms (pistol, rifle used as a club)

mobility: On foot; no special mobility documented
limitations: Lacks superhuman physical durability or regenerative healing

sources.supports: Nakia as a War Dog spy, her undercover trafficking-convoy mission, Ring Blades and firearms, the casino fight, and her fight at Mount Bashenga where she disarmed Killmonger but was wounded and thrown aside.

feats.claim: Fought at Mount Bashenga against Killmonger's side, defeating several Border Tribe warriors.
While undercover among a trafficking convoy's captives, slipped out when Black Panther attacked and helped him fight the soldiers with a seized machine gun; the captives were freed.
Disarmed Erik Killmonger with her Ring Blades during the Mount Bashenga battle.

notableResults.note: She disarmed him with her Ring Blades, but he wounded her thigh with his suit's claws and threw her aside.

campaignTags.claim: Went undercover in Nigeria posing as a Nigerian woman inside a trafficking convoy; her cover held until T'Challa intervened.

unknowns: Exact extent of her post-Blip covert missions before returning in Wakanda Forever (the MCU Wiki page as read did not cover Wakanda Forever).
Whether her Ring Blades' energy charge comes from technology or skill is unclear on the source page.

characters.summary: Namor is the mutant ruler of Talokan who breathes both air and water, flies with ankle wings, and has superhuman strength, but weakens when dried out.

techniques: Stabbing strikes (stabbed Shuri through the abdomen)

mechanisms: Superhuman durability (survived a close-range explosion set off by Shuri, though badly hurt)

weaknesses: Drying him out weakens him; Shuri and Riri trapped him in a ship and turned up the heat to dehydrate him
limitations: His strength drops when he is out of water long enough to dry out

sources.supports: MCU Namor born a mutant able to breathe air and water, can fly, has super strength, and is slowed when dried out.
Final Shuri vs Namor fight: Shuri and Riri trap him in a heated ship, crash in the desert, Shuri cuts off an ankle wing, he stabs her, she injures him with an explosion, and he yields.
Namor's mutations make him adept at swimming, fighting and flying; he surrenders to Shuri after the fight.

feats.claim: Stabbed Shuri (powered by the Heart-Shaped Herb) through the abdomen while weakened by dehydration.
Survived an explosion Shuri set off at close range, though seriously hurt.

notableResults.note: Shuri and Riri lured him into a ship heated to dry him out and crashed it in the desert; Shuri cut off one ankle wing and, after he stabbed her, injured him with an explosion. He yielded.

campaignTags.claim: Can fly by his own mutation, using ankle wings.
Born a mutant able to breathe both air and water.
His mutations make him remarkably adept at swimming.

unknowns: The MCU Wiki Namor page could not be fetched (site error); claims rest on Looper and GamesRadar.
Lifting/throwing feats (the original 'hurled masonry and military equipment' claim) and use of a spear are not supported by any page read; removed.
Exact upper limits of his strength compared to other heavy-hitters.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, Earth-616 (Avengers vs. X-Men, 2012). Comics form only; not shown in the MCU. Attached to the MCU Namor roster entry by the game.
characters.summary: In Avengers vs. X-Men, Namor became one of the Phoenix Five when Iron Man's weapon split the Phoenix Force; empowered by his fragment he flooded Wakanda and fought the assembled Avengers until he was defeated and his share was taken by the other four.

techniques: Commanding a giant wave / wall of water to flood a city
Energy blasts (traded blasts with the Scarlet Witch)

mechanisms: Phoenix Force fragment empowerment; kept fighting after a strike from Thor's Mjolnir

weaknesses: Chaos Magic: the Phoenix is weak to it, and the Scarlet Witch's blasts brought him down
characters.formDifferences: Base Namor plus a fifth of the Phoenix Force: levitation, control of a city-drowning wave, Phoenix burning attacks and enough power to fight a dozen Avengers at once. He loses the fragment when defeated (it was absorbed by the other Phoenix Five). The MCU has not shown this form.

sources.supports: Namor becomes one of five Phoenix avatars in AvX, raises a massive wall of water to drown Wakanda, is defeated by the combined Avengers and his share is absorbed by the other Phoenix Five.

Synopsis of Phoenix Namor's attack on Wakanda: levitates, commands a giant wave, breaks Red Hulk's arm, burns the Avengers, is hit by Mjolnir, trades blasts with the Scarlet Witch (Phoenix weak to Chaos Magic) and falls defeated.

unknowns: Neither page lists the full set of abilities the Phoenix fragment granted; the original 'reality manipulation', 'planetary-scale telekinesis' and 'near-absolute invulnerability' claims are unsupported and were removed.
Not an MCU form; the MCU has never shown Namor with the Phoenix Force.

feats.claim: Raised a massive wall of water from a lake that flooded and destroyed almost all of Wakanda.
Broke Red Hulk's arm and burned a dozen attacking Avengers.

notableResults.opponent: Avengers (incl. Scarlet Witch, Thor, Red Hulk, Black Panther)
notableResults.note: Fought the Avengers in Wakanda; traded blasts with the Scarlet Witch, whose Chaos Magic the Phoenix is weak to, and fell defeated. The other Phoenix Five then took his fragment.

campaignTags.claim: Levitates above Wakanda while empowered by the Phoenix.
Commands a giant wave that floods Wakanda.
Burns the attacking Avengers with Phoenix power.

characters.summary: Nebula is a cyborg assassin raised by Thanos, with a cybernetic arm and eye, a memory-recording synaptic drive and a regeneration implant, fighting with electroshock batons and blasters; she is also a skilled pilot.

techniques: Cybernetic arm with retractable claws and grappling hook

mechanisms: Regeneration implant that rapidly heals near-fatal injuries
Cybernetic limb replacement (replaced a lost hand)

weaknesses: Her cybernetic memory systems can be accessed: Ebony Maw examined her memory network and Thanos viewed her memories and played them through her implants
limitations: Lost limbs do not regrow; she replaces them with cybernetics

sources.supports: Nebula's cybernetics (arm, eye, synaptic drive, regeneration implant), weapons, piloting, fights with Gamora and Thanos, Thanos reading her memories, and her role in the Battle of Earth.

feats.claim: Fought Gamora repeatedly; on Xandar she disarmed Gamora and nearly electrocuted her to death.
Escaped after being knocked off a ship by cutting off her own hand, later replacing it with a cybernetic one.
Sided with the Avengers and fought alongside Gamora in the Battle of Earth.

notableResults.note: After disarming Gamora on Xandar she was knocked off the ship and escaped only by cutting off her hand.
On Ego's planet Nebula had Gamora in a chokehold but let her go; Gamora said she had not truly lost, and the sisters reconciled.
Nebula proved no match for Thanos.

campaignTags.claim: Has a cybernetic arm, bionic eye and implanted synaptic drive.
Uses electroshock batons, an electric blaster, and an arm with a grappling hook that can hack computer systems.
Electroshock batons and an electric blaster that stuns or kills.
A highly trained pilot; flew an M-Ship from Xandar and the Benatar with Rocket.
A regeneration implant lets her rapidly heal from near-fatal injuries.

unknowns: Full limit of her resistance to high-yield thermal energy attacks.
The source is inconsistent about which Nebula shot her 2014 self in Endgame; not used as a feat.

characters.summary: Ned Leeds is Peter Parker's best friend, a hacker and science enthusiast who in No Way Home picks up a Sling Ring and opens portals almost instantly with no training.

techniques: Improvised use of Peter's gear (distracted Shocker with a web-shooter)

weaknesses: Standard human physical attributes with zero formal martial combat training
limitations: Lacks combat durability and offensive spells beyond opening portals

sources.supports: Ned's background as Peter Parker's friend, hacker and science enthusiast, and distracting Shocker with a web-shooter; this page does not cover No Way Home.
Ned uses the Sling Ring to open portals almost instantly with no training, surprising Doctor Strange; his grandmother said he might have magic in him.
Ned's Sling Ring portals bring in two alternate Peter Parkers and accidentally free Doctor Strange from the Mirror Dimension.

feats.claim: Opened Sling Ring portals that brought two alternate Peter Parkers into his universe.
Mastered Sling Ring portals almost instantly with no training, surprising Doctor Strange.
Distracted Shocker with one of Peter's web-shooters to save Peter.

conditional.dependsOn: Possession and use of a Sling Ring

campaignTags.claim: Opens portals with a Sling Ring.
His portal ability comes from using Doctor Strange's Sling Ring.
His portals brought two alternate Peter Parkers to his location.

unknowns: Whether he has innate magic (his grandmother said he might) or will pursue mystic arts training.
No spellcasting beyond Sling Ring portals is documented in the pages read.

characters.summary: Nick Fury is a master strategist, spy, and former Director of S.H.I.E.L.D. who relies on firearms, tactical planning, and vast governmental resources.

techniques: Handguns and heavy firearms (including a rocket launcher)

mechanisms: Armored SUV defenses and the Mouse Hole escape cutter

limitations: Vulnerable to conventional physical injury and assassination

sources.supports: Nick Fury's S.H.I.E.L.D. career, the Washington D.C. ambush and faked death, the Avengers Initiative's origin, his gadgets, undercover work, helicopter flight at the Triskelion, and fights with Talos, Pierce and Gravik.

feats.claim: Survived a HYDRA ambush in Washington D.C.: after the Winter Soldier disabled his SUV with a disc grenade, he cut through the car with the Mouse Hole and escaped into the sewers.
Founded what became the Avengers Initiative (first the Protectors Initiative) after meeting Carol Danvers, and reactivated it after Loki's invasion.
Faked his death with Tetrodotoxin B after being shot by the Winter Soldier.

notableResults.note: After escaping the vehicle ambush, Fury was shot twice through the wall of Steve Rogers's apartment; he survived by faking his death.
Overpowered by Talos; Vers stunned Talos.

campaignTags.claim: Flew a helicopter out of the Triskelion battle, letting Sam Wilson jump aboard.
Uses the Mouse Hole cutter, a transmitter pager and his SUV's built-in weapons.
Posed as an undercover operative and lifted a fingerprint with tape to get into the Joint Dark Energy Mission Facility.

unknowns: Full extent of his S.A.B.E.R. space-station defense capabilities.
Only the first 100,000 of 175,632 characters of the source page were read.

characters.summary: Obadiah Stane is a ruthless Stark Industries executive with no superhuman powers who fights in the Iron Monger, a giant armor built from the Mark I design and powered by Tony Stark's stolen arc reactor.

techniques: Arm-mounted 23mm Gatling gun and rotary grenade launcher

mechanisms: Heavy Omnium Steel Iron Monger armor

weaknesses: Ices up and shuts down at upper-atmosphere temperatures
Key mechanics and wiring are exposed on the exterior; Stark tore out its optical circuits
mobility: Flight jets (short jumps or sustained flight)
limitations: Without the Iron Monger suit, he possesses standard human physical limits

sources.supports: Obadiah Stane's MCU Wiki page (titled Iron Monger): no superhuman abilities, the suit's weapons and jets, the stolen arc reactor, the icing weakness, and his defeat in the reactor overload.
Iron Monger Armor specs: several times larger than the Iron Man suit, chest cockpit, 7.5-ton lift per arm, weapons, flight jets, icing and exposed-systems weaknesses, and the final fight.

feats.claim: Pursued Iron Man into the upper atmosphere in the Iron Monger armor.
Fought Tony Stark in the Mark III armor.

notableResults.note: Stark ripped out his optical circuits, then Pepper Potts overloaded the large arc reactor on Stark's order; Stane was electrocuted and fell into the reactor.

campaignTags.claim: Wears the Iron Monger, an arc-reactor-powered armor with flight jets and integrated weapons.
The Iron Monger armor is several times larger than the Iron Man suit.
The armor's flight jets can reconfigure for sustained flight; he chased Iron Man into the upper atmosphere.

unknowns: Exact height of the Iron Monger armor is not given on the pages read.
The two MCU Wiki pages disagree on whether he picked up or threw a car of civilians in the main-continuity fight; the claim is not used.
Whether he built any suits besides the Iron Monger (none mentioned).

characters.summary: Odin is the Allfather of Asgard, wielding immense cosmic-level magic, divine strength, and the power of the Odinforce.

techniques: Odinforce energy blasts channelled through Gungnir
Enchantments (the worthiness enchantment on Mjolnir) and banishments

mechanisms: Asgardian physiology (superhuman strength and regenerative healing)

weaknesses: Helpless while in the Odinsleep; Laufey nearly stabbed him as he slept
limitations: Must periodically enter the Odinsleep to rest and maintain his power

sources.supports: Odin's status as Allfather, the Odinforce, Gungnir energy blasts, the Mjolnir enchantment and Thor's banishment, conquest with Hela and her banishment, the Odinsleep, and riding Sleipnir.

feats.claim: Stripped Thor of his power, enchanted Mjolnir so only the worthy could wield it, and sent both to Earth.
Conquered the Nine Realms alongside Hela, then banished her to Hel, binding his life force to her prison.

campaignTags.claim: Placed the worthiness enchantment on Mjolnir and cast Thor's exile.
Channels the Odinforce through Gungnir to fire energy blasts.
Rode Sleipnir, his eight-legged steed, to rescue Thor.

unknowns: Full extent of his power output at his absolute historical prime.

The MCU Wiki describes Odin beating Laufey in single combat and defeating Hela and Surtur, but gives no film citation; these may come from tie-ins rather than films or Disney+ series, so they are not listed as results.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, Earth-616 (Thor #300, 1980; Mighty Thor Vol. 2 #1). Comics form only; in the MCU Odin commands the Destroyer remotely and never wears it. Attached to the MCU Odin roster entry by the game.
characters.summary: In the comics, Odin built the enchanted Destroyer armor to fight the Celestials, absorbed the life forces of the Asgardians (except Thor) and entered it to face the Fourth Host; the armor was melted down. He later used the Destroyer to enforce his rule as a tyrant.

techniques: Visor beam that can disintegrate nearly any substance
Energy bolts said to shatter planets

mechanisms: Armor described as practically impervious to physical damage, tougher than adamantium and uru

weaknesses: The visor must stay open to charge its most powerful beam
characters.formDifferences: Odin's spirit (with the absorbed life forces of the Asgardians) inhabits the enchanted Destroyer: Class 100+ strength, Mach 32 flight, planet-shattering energy bolts, a disintegrating visor beam, matter manipulation and near-total durability. Leaving his body behind, he fights as the armor.

sources.supports: Comics Destroyer: built by Odin to fight the Celestials, entered by Odin with the Asgardians' life forces for the Fourth Host (Thor #300) and melted down, later used by tyrant Odin (Mighty Thor Vol. 2 #1); armor powers.
MCU Destroyer: operated remotely by whoever holds Gungnir (Odin, later Loki); the page does not say Odin ever wore it.

unknowns: Not an MCU form: in the MCU, Odin only commands the Destroyer remotely through Gungnir.
Some armor powers (matter manipulation, the life-force passage) have no citation on the source page.
What happened to Odin's spirit at the moment the armor was melted is not stated on the page read.

feats.claim: Entered the Destroyer carrying the combined life forces of the Asgardians to face the Celestials' Fourth Host.
Used the Destroyer Armor to enforce his rule as a tyrant after the Odinson disappeared.

notableResults.note: The armor failed against the Celestials and was melted down; Thor later had the Skyfathers restore Odin.

campaignTags.claim: The Destroyer is an armor Odin enchanted with his magic, infused with the Skyfathers' power.
The armor flies at up to Mach 32.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, Earth-616 (Marvel Legacy #1, 2017; Avengers Vol. 8, 2018-). Comics form only; the MCU has not shown a prehistoric Avengers team. Attached to the MCU Odin roster entry by the game.
characters.summary: In the comics, a young Odin, still learning to control Mjolnir, joined Firehair (the Phoenix) in forming the Avengers of 1,000,000 BC to protect early humanity, fighting the fallen Celestial and the Celestials' First Host.

techniques: Wielding Mjolnir (which he initially struggled to control)

mechanisms: Asgardian god physiology (era-specific durability not documented)

characters.formDifferences: A young Odin before his reign, wielding Mjolnir (and still struggling to control it) as a member of the Stone Age Avengers, rather than the older Allfather with Gungnir and the Odinforce.

sources.supports: The 1,000,000 BC Avengers: Firehair recruits Odin, the team subdues Zgreb the Aspirant and buries it in South Africa, loses to the Celestials' First Host, and later splits over Odin's treatment of Phoenix.
Odin initially struggling to control Mjolnir and forming the Stone Age Avengers to fight the Fallen (Marvel Legacy #1).
MCU Odin page: only a trivia note that comics Odin was one of the first Ancient Avengers; no MCU appearance of this form.

unknowns: Neither page describes young Odin's individual powers, armor or fighting style in this era; the original 'early Odinforce bursts', 'spear combat' and 'overconfidence' claims are unsupported and were removed.
Exact issue for the First Host battle is not given on the page read.
Not an MCU form.

feats.claim: Helped subdue the out-of-control Celestial known as the Fallen (Zgreb the Aspirant) and seal it underground in what is now South Africa.

notableResults.note: Team victory with the 1,000,000 BC Avengers; Odin wanted to nail it to the Moon but it was buried instead.
Team loss; the Celestials spared the Avengers as useful against the Horde.

campaignTags.claim: Wielded Mjolnir, though he initially struggled to control it.
